---
title: "SAE Toolkit"
subtitle: "Bring your own survey into the workflow"
---

This SAE toolkit provides templates for preparing survey and auxiliary data, a decision framework for choosing an appropriate SAE method, and method-specific scripts with the expected inputs and outputs.

## Define the estimands and estimation domain

Start by defining the estimand:

- what outcome is being estimated;
- who is in the target population;
- at which spatial scale;
- over which time periods.

In a spatio-temporal SAE workflow, the target estimate is produced for every area-by-period combination estimation domain. Each is an **area-time cell**.

## Prepare the modelling input

Prepare the inputs according to the route chosen in the flowchart. All methods need a defined area-time grid. Other inputs depend on whether the method uses direct estimates, unit-level modelling, area summaries, or poststratification.

### Domain frame

Always prepare a domain frame. It has one row for every area-time cell that should receive an estimate and stores the numeric indices used by `INLA`.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area to estimate |
| `time_id` | Time period to estimate |
| `area_inla_id` | Numeric area index for `INLA` |
| `time_inla_id` | Numeric time index for `INLA` |
| labels | Optional area or period labels for display |

### Spatial graph

Prepare a spatial graph if the selected model includes spatial random effects.

| File | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `*.adj` | `INLA` adjacency graph, ordered by `area_inla_id` |

### Survey input

Prepare one row per respondent-period for the outcome being estimated.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unit_id` | Respondent identifier |
| `area_id` | Area assigned to the respondent |
| `time_id` | Survey period |
| `outcome` | Outcome used in estimation, either binary or continuous |
| `weight` | Survey design weight |
| `strata` | Survey stratum, if available |
| `unitpred_*` | Unit-level predictors, required for unit-level SAE |

### Area-level predictors or summaries

Prepare one row per area. This table is used for area-level SAE, and unit-level SAE with area summaries, if applicable.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area identifier |
| `areapred_*` | Raw area-level predictors |
| `*_mean` / `*_share` | Area summaries of `unitpred_*`, required for unit-level SAE with area summaries |

### Poststratification data

Required for unit-level SAE with poststratification. The population cells must match the categorical `unitpred_*` variables used in the poststratified unit-level model.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Area identifier |
| `time_id` | Time period |
| population groups | Categories used for poststratification; must match `unitpred_*` |
| `pop_count` | Population count for each cell |

## Expected outputs

After each method, convert outputs to a common comparison schema so estimates can be compared, mapped, and joined back to other urban datasets.

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Estimated area |
| `time_id` | Estimated period |
| `estimate` | Direct or model-based point estimate |
| `variance` | Sampling or posterior variance |
| `lower`, `upper` | Uncertainty interval bounds |
| `ci_width` | Uncertainty interval width |
| `n` | Sample size |
| `remarks` | Estimation method, model specification or other notes |
